- a conservative estimate of tokens/sec the reserved slab will guarantee under our 95th p95 latencies for the 13B model we demoed,

Hi Alyssa —

Appreciate the context. I put together a short hypothesis workbook (attached) and a recommended dual-path slab plan. High-level summary up front:

- Conservative committed TPS recommendation: 55 tokens/sec sustained per slab (dedicated pool node set) to meet 200ms p95 on the 13B baseline we tested with your prompt mix.
- Expected latency ranges at 55 TPS (13B quantized): p50 ~45ms, p95 ~180–220ms depending on tokenization and KV cache hit-rate.
- Minimum headroom: 30% compute buffer recommended for Q4 traffic variance; 45% if Voyant requires strict p95 guardrails during marketing-driven spikes.

What I attached:
- voyant_commit_coverage_workbook.xlsx — scenario tabs: baseline, 30pct_headroom, 45pct_headroom, burst-simulation. Each tab includes tokens/sec -> GPU slab mapping and estimated p95 latency.
- draft-sla-v1.pdf — short statement of recommended SLO wording and fallback behavior (regional fallback + smaller model variant).

A few notes on assumptions in the workbook:
- Model: quantized 13B (int8) tuned matching your prompt-length distribution (median prompt 80 tokens).
- Typical sequence length used: request 120 tokens + response 60 tokens (per call ~= 180 tokens).
- Caching: prefix-level KV cache assumed 40% hit-rate in steady state; if you can prewarm common prompts this materially reduces p95.
- Batching: continuous batching at 100ms aggregation window; we recommend conservative 50ms for user-facing with strict latency targets, which reduces throughput vs larger batch windows.

Next steps I propose:
1) Kimberly to run a quick sensitivity from the workbook with your exact prompt histogram (if you share a sample).
2) Ben to sketch the minimal Dedicated slab configuration (GPU SKU mix + node counts) for the 30% headroom case and a 45% elevated-headroom case.
3) We sync Tue to finalize numbers for procurement.

Kimberly / Ben — tagging you here to pick up the sensitivity + hardware mapping.

-David
Head of Capacity Strategy | Redwood Inference

FYI — forwarding the initial ask. I ran the first-pass sensitivity using the median prompt length you supplied and the traffic multipliers Alyssa mentioned. Key outputs pasted below.

Summary (first pass):
- Baseline (no headroom): 55 TPS ~ maps to 4x A100-style GPUs (dedicated slab) for your request/response mix (180 tokens avg).
- 30% headroom: recommend 6x GPU-equivalent capacity (slab = 4 + 2 buffer nodes) -> sustained 71 TPS effective commitment.
- 45% headroom: recommend 7x GPU-equivalent capacity -> sustained 80 TPS effective commitment.

Estimated p95 latency (engineering sim):
- 55 TPS: 160–220ms (depends on KV cache hit; cold-start tails can spike to 350ms).
- 71 TPS: 200–300ms (some variance in tail).
- 80 TPS: 220–360ms (risk of >300ms p95 under cold starts).

Risk notes:
- If Voyant's spike factor (6x) happens during a cold-start window, p95 will breach 200ms unless we trigger regional fallback to a smaller quantized 7B variant.
- Autoscale bump times and our guaranteed slab burst policy need to be in the SLA if you want a hard p95 cap.

I'll produce a simple slab SKU mapping (A100/RTX/other quantized SKU equivalents) and an ops playbook for fallback triggers. Ben — can you add the node counts + cost delta for each slab option?

-Kimberly
